label: copy-phase input p (fed-back p), strongest in short sequences near the end
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L) when the fed-back input token is p: 99.4% of activation mass is on in_tok == p, and it never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>. It does not fire on every copy-phase p, though. Magnitude is modulated by position: it is strongest in short sequences (L 3-6 hold about 88% of the mass) and when few outputs are left (to_go <= 2 holds about 91%). Repeated p in the original also boosts it (top examples like p p r, and higher rate for in_count >= 2). Copy-phase p early in long sequences (L >= 7, many outputs left) is mostly inactive. Plain (phase==2)&(in_tok==p) has recall 0.98 but precision 0.26. Adding L<=6 & to_go<=3 brings dev F1 to 0.67 (P 0.59, R 0.76, mass recall 0.87). The leftover gating is graded, so no simple threshold cleanly captures it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: p, 3, r, k, b, j; least: x, v, w, c) and the token being output (most: p, r, 3, k, 2, o; least: x, v, c, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, recall_idx=3, L=3 & t=4.
